links.targetTitle: Cross-chain USDC movement depends on Circle's CCTP under a d

title: CCTP transfers are metered by a global limit and a per-destination limit simultaneously
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.15.1.2 charges two limits for one action:

```
rateLimited(LIMIT_USDC_TO_CCTP, usdcAmount);
rateLimited(makeDomainKey(LIMIT_USDC_TO_DOMAIN, destinationDomain), usdcAmount);
```

The two answer different questions. The global key bounds how much USDC Grove may push out of the origin chain in total, which is a liquidity and operational-risk question about Grove. The domain key bounds how much may go to any single destination, which is a concentration question about that chain and its bridge-side deployment.

Neither subsumes the other. A generous global limit with tight per-domain limits allows large aggregate rebalancing while capping exposure to any one chain's failure. Tight global with generous per-domain allows a full allocation to be sent anywhere but not much of it in total. Governance can tune the two independently as new chains are added, without recalibrating existing corridors.

The cost is that both budgets must be provisioned and maintained, and an operation can now fail for two different reasons that look identical to a relayer. In exchange, the limit registry expresses a genuinely two-dimensional risk surface rather than flattening it into one number.
description: Both LIMIT_USDC_TO_CCTP and the domain-keyed LIMIT_USDC_TO_DOMAIN must admit the amount, so total bridging capacity and per-corridor capacity are independently governable.
